claims.title: Graph signing: current negative, bipartite constructor and promised-base interfaces

quoted_fields.interface: Real signed adjacency matrices with ONE shared sign per original unoriented edge. The promised-base interfaces here use explicit connected simple d-regular graphs with d>=3, r=2sqrt(d-1), and all nontrivial unsigned eigenvalues in[-r,r]. For a bipartite graph the trivial -d mode is also removed. Imported primary statements retain their own governing hypotheses; this card uses their d>=3 regular-graph subcases and does not claim those papers are limited to regular inputs.
quoted_fields.failure: The GENERAL sharp-signing claim is already FALSE at the cubic counterexample scope; the counterexample is NOT Ramanujan and therefore does not settle promised-Ramanujan-base closure. Prescribed bipartite sharp signing HAS a deterministic polynomial-BIT constructor at the current source version. A stronger existential coefficient is not a signing-selection algorithm. One bad mixed-root-good signing is not an all-signings counterexample. Local repair/cut/embedding failures and exact norm tests are not a full constructor or full negative for promised bases. The original matrix-variance target N1768 is different and remains unresolved at its own scope. Historical P-graph fixed-degree graphs-from-size are not prescribed-base closure; the newly screened OpenAI graph-from-size original remains Root-unread/metadata-only and held originals are not recovered. Root read the declared theorem/proof sections, not every seed lemma or all papers in full; no new Capital primary acquisition, independent reproof, novelty audit or graph execution.
